name: SC-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+21 partisan lean strongly favors Republicans
Incumbent Biggs running with large fundraising edge
Polymarket prices Biggs near 95% to win
Democrat Lehmacher raised under $100K with no outside support
model.rationale: The R+21 lean, Biggs's incumbency and roughly five-to-one fundraising advantage, and markets pricing her near 95% all point to a safe Republican hold. No polls or expert ratings exist, so the forecast rests on fundamentals, which show only a modest Democratic environment offsetting the district's tilt.
model.watch: Any late polling or outside spending in the district would be the first sign the race is closer than fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Carolina's 3rd District is a solidly Republican seat, and first-term incumbent Sheri Biggs is seeking reelection after winning renomination. The district's partisan lean of roughly R+21 makes a Democratic takeover a steep climb in any environment.

Democrat Eunice Lehmacher has raised under $100,000 and has no outside support, while Biggs has raised over $500,000 and holds a large cash advantage. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give Biggs about a 95% chance of winning. The forecast expects Biggs to win by a wide, roughly nineteen-point margin, with the Democratic environment providing only a small offset to the district's strong Republican tilt.
